en: The Ritual Manual for the Secret Mantra of the Threefold Siddhis of the Three Bodies of the Buddha, the Heart of Uṣṇīṣavijayā, which Shatters Hell, Transforms Karmic Obstructions,
and Exits the Triple World, in One Scroll.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of Central India by Imperial Decree: The Mahāvairocana Tathāgata proclaimed this from the Golden Drum; as his mouth opened and his tongue was raised, it shook the palaces of the Dharma-realm. The Tathāgatas of the Lotus-womb World-system emerged from meditative equipoise, and immediately, in order to shatter the hells and extinguish the calamities of the seven cycles of rebirth, they initiated the teaching for Bodhisattvas by proclaiming the five-syllable secret mantra. These five syllables are: A, Vaṃ, Raṃ, Haṃ, Khaṃ.

The syllable A belongs to the Vajra family and presides over the liver; the syllable Vaṃ belongs to the Lotus family and presides over the lungs; the syllable Raṃ belongs to the Jewel family and presides over the heart; the syllable Haṃ belongs to the Karma family and presides over the stomach; the syllable Khaṃ belongs to the Space family and presides over the spleen.

Mountains, seas, and the great earth emerge from the letter *A*; rivers and the myriad streams emerge from the letter *Vaṃ*; gold, jade, precious gems, the sun, moon, stars, fire-pearls, and radiant light are formed from the letter *Raṃ*; the five grains, five fruits, and the blooming of various flowers are brought to fruition by the letter *Haṃ*; and the cultivation of fragrance, beautiful persons, the long life of gods and humans, their complexions, flavors, upright features, merit, virtue, wealth, and nobility are adorned by the letter *Kṣaṃ*.

The syllable A is the Tathāgata Akṣobhya of the eastern direction; the syllable Vaṃ is the Tathāgata Amitābha of the western direction; the syllable Raṃ is the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava of the southern direction; the syllable Haṃ is the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi of the northern direction; and the syllable Khaṃ is the Tathāgata Vairocana Mahāvairocana of the zenith.

The meaning of the letter A is the essence of profound emptiness and stillness; it cannot be grasped, nor can it be relinquished. It is the mother of all phenomena—the letter A, the Great King of Empowerment.
This Dharma is difficult to believe; let the Vinaya masters of the Hīnayāna especially not see this original text.

This fifty-character mantra—the supreme field of merit—is extracted from the forty-thousand-verse Sanskrit manuscript of the *Vairocana Sūtra* and gathers the most essential and subtle points of the *Vajraśekhara Sūtra*. The merit obtained by those who recite it is incomparable, inconceivable, and ineffable.

Contemplating the principle of suchness brings forth blessings: one’s physical frame becomes firm and robust, forever free from calamities, obstacles, and the suffering of disease, thereby sustaining a long life.

If these five characters are inscribed upon a drum, the sound of the drum struck by those who read the inscription will be heard far and wide, spreading intensely for a thousand li; the crops will receive abundant nourishment, and the people will be free from disasters and pestilence. This is the contemplation of the non-arising nature of this Tathāgata.

These five sections of mantras are the precious nectar and supreme cream of the non-arising ambrosia of all Tathāgatas, and the wondrous medicine of Buddha-nature. When even a single character enters the five viscera, ten thousand ailments do not arise; how much more so when one cultivates the contemplation of the sun and the contemplation of the moon, whereby one immediately realizes the emptiness and stillness of the Buddha-body.

These five syllables—A, VAṂ, RAṂ, HAṂ, KHAṂ—are the dharmakāya mantra. If one recites them once, seven times, twenty-one times, or forty-nine times each day, the merit calculated from such practice is equal to that of reciting all the sūtras one million times for every single recitation.

How much more so when, in the stillness of meditation, one enters the gate of samādhi and contemplates the letter A with clear and distinct discernment, like the sun shining upon the sky; this is the direct realization of the Buddha-nature, and the merit obtained therein is beyond measure.

The phrases of this Secret Treasury are truly inconceivable; I only fear that the Dharma-preachers among the śrāvakas and those who uphold the Vinaya of the Hīnayāna will give rise to doubts and lack faith, which would conversely increase their transgressions.

For example, suppose a king has a youngest son whom he especially cherishes; he would exhaust his treasury and storehouses of precious jewels without regret, yet he would not give him the swords Ganjiang and Moye, fearing that because the boy does not understand how to wield them, he might injure his own body.
Therefore, the Tathāgata’s secret transmission is for the great bodhisattvas and not for those with the inferior wisdom of the śrāvakas.

In the first section, the *Akṣaravajrabhūmi*, one performs the visualization of the ground and the visualization of the vajra-seat based on the single syllable *A*. Its form is four-cornered and its color is yellow; it is the Great Perfect Mirror Wisdom (*ādarśajñāna*), also known as Vajra Wisdom.

Regarding the two syllables *vaṃ* of the Water Family of Vajra: one should visualize the syllable *vaṃ* as water and as a lotus flower. Its form is like the full moon and it is white in color; it is the Wondrous Observational Wisdom (*pratyavekṣaṇā-jñāna*), also known as the Lotus Wisdom and the Wisdom of Turning the Wheel of Dharma (*dharmacakra-pravartana-jñāna*).

Contemplate the syllable *laṃ* of the Vajra Fire Family as the sun; it is triangular in shape and red in color, representing the Wisdom of Equality (*samatājñāna*), also known as the Wisdom of Consecration (*abhiṣekajñāna*).

Contemplate the syllable *haṃ* of the Vajra Wind Family as the moon; it is shaped like a crescent moon and black in color, representing the Wisdom of Accomplishing What Is to Be Done (*kṛtyānuṣṭhānajñāna*), also known as the Wisdom of Ritual Action (*karmajñāna*).

Regarding the five syllables *aṃ*, *vaṃ*, *laṃ*, *haṃ*, and *kṣaṃ* of the Vajra-Emptiness Family, one performs the visualization of emptiness; their form is like that of the full moon, representing the wisdom of the nature of the various *dharmadhātus*.

These are the seed-syllables of the five wheels: earth, water, fire, wind, and space. Among these five syllables—*aṃ*, *vaṃ*, *laṃ*, *haṃ*, and *kṣaṃ*—the syllable *aṃ* represents the earth wheel. Above the earth wheel is the water wheel; above the water wheel is the fire wheel; above the fire wheel is the wind wheel; and above the wind wheel is the space wheel.
Within the wind-circle, one visualizes the syllable *haṃ*, which is deep and dark blue in color; it gradually expands and widens.

Above the wind-circle, one visualizes the syllable *vaṃ*, which transforms into the water-circle. Above that, one visualizes the syllable *pra*, golden in color, which transforms into a single golden tortoise. Upon its back, one visualizes the syllable *su*, which immediately becomes Mount Sumeru, the King of Mountains, composed of the four jewels. Furthermore, the syllable *ja* transforms into a mountain of gold, surrounding [Mount Sumeru] in seven tiers.

Visualize within the void that from the pores of the body of Vairocana Buddha, fragrant milk flows forth, raining down upon the intervals between the seven golden mountains to form an ocean of fragrant milk-water possessing the eight meritorious qualities.

One should visualize that upon the summit of Mount Sumeru is the auspicious syllable *hrīḥ*, which transforms into an eight-petaled lotus pervading the entire dharma-realm. Upon this lotus is the syllable *a*, which transforms into a precious pavilion with eight flowers and eight pillars; it is high and vast, without center or periphery, and adorned with various kinds of sublime and wondrous jewels.

Sixty koṭis of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, along with the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings, and the bodhisattvas who offer internal and external worship, surrounded this palace within the Dharma-realm.

Furthermore, there is the syllable-gateway *Ri*, which transforms into a great lotus petal. Upon it is a maṇḍala; within the maṇḍala is a lion throne; upon the lion throne is a king of lotuses; above that is a pure full moon disc; and upon the full moon disc is the syllable *Giri*, which transforms into a wondrous moon-like great lotus. Above this is the syllable *Vaṃ*, which emits a great radiance that universally illumines the entire Dharma-realm. All sentient beings within the three realms, the six destinies, the four modes of birth, and the eight difficulties who are suffering, upon encountering the touch of this light, attain liberation.

This syllable *vaṃ* transforms into a *stūpa*, which is square, circular, triangular, crescent-shaped, and spherical, because it is composed of the five great elements: earth, water, fire, wind, and space.

This stūpa transforms into the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, whose body is moon-colored and who wears a crown of five Buddhas upon his head. His body is adorned with exquisite *dukūla* celestial garments and necklaces, and his radiance universally illuminates the dharma-realm of the ten directions. He rests upon a lunar disc, surrounded by a retinue consisting of the four Buddhas, the four Pāramitās, the sixteen [Bodhisattvas], the eight offerings, the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*), the thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa, the twenty heavens, and immeasurable, boundless Bodhisattvas.

As for the four Buddhas: Akṣobhya Buddha is the *svābhāvikakāya* (essential body) of adamantine solidity; Ratnasambhava Buddha is the *saṃbhogakāya* (enjoyment body) adorned with merit; Amitābha Buddha is the *jñānakāya* (wisdom body) of enjoyment; and Śākyamuni Buddha is the *nirmāṇakāya* (emanation body) of transformation.
The four bodhisattvas are Vajrapāramitā Bodhisattva, Ratnapāramitā Bodhisattva, Dharmapāramitā Bodhisattva, and Karmapāramitā Bodhisattva.

The sixteen bodhisattvas are: Vajrasattva Bodhisattva, Vajrarāja Bodhisattva, Vajrarāga Bodhisattva, Vajrasādhu Bodhisattva, Vajraratna Bodhisattva, Vajraprabha Bodhisattva, Vajraketu Bodhisattva, Vajrahāsa Bodhisattva, Vajradharma Bodhisattva, Vajratīkṣṇa Bodhisattva, Vajrahetu Bodhisattva, Vajrabhāṣa Bodhisattva, Vajrakarma Bodhisattva, Vajrarakṣa Bodhisattva, Vajradaṃṣṭra Bodhisattva, and Vajramuṣṭi Bodhisattva.

The eight offering Bodhisattvas are: Vajralāsyā Bodhisattva, Vajramālā Bodhisattva, Vajragītā Bodhisattva, Vajranṛtyā Bodhisattva, Vajradhūpā Bodhisattva, Vajrapuṣpā Bodhisattva, Vajradīpā Bodhisattva, and Vajragandhā Bodhisattva.
The four bodhisattvas who perform the means of attraction are Vajrāṅkuśa Bodhisattva, Vajrapāśa Bodhisattva, Vajrasphoṭa Bodhisattva, and Vajraghaṇṭā Bodhisattva.

Having thus contemplated such a retinue, by realizing the purity of mind, one’s own mind becomes the Buddha, with all marks fully perfected; one then realizes *sarbajñā* (all-knowledge) and possesses the complete assembly of the thirty-seven noble deities. Then, one contemplates within space that all Buddhas are as pervasive as sesame seeds throughout the realm of empty space.

Visualize that one’s own body realizes the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*); the syllable *VAṂ* transforms into the water of great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*). Imagine sprinkling this upon the great earth of the bodhicitta of myself and all sentient beings, washing away the stains of the sixty-one conceptual proliferations (*prapañca*) of the mind. Thus, all afflictions and karmic defilements are utterly severed, and while not abandoning this very body born of one’s parents, one manifests in this life to realize the state of the fruit of Buddhahood, Great Enlightenment (*mahābodhi*).
Furthermore, one contemplates that within the body there is a great ocean; at its bottom is the letter *pra*, golden in color, which transforms into a golden tortoise—this is the Buddha-nature.

Upon that tortoise was the letter SU, which transformed into Mount Sumeru, the King of Mountains. Upon that mountain was the letter A, which transformed into a subtle vajra-ground wheel of various colors. Upon the wheel was a site of practice (maṇḍala) measuring thirty-eight cubits.
The syllable *Aṃ* transforms into a three-tiered maṇi-jewel palace, which is the realm of desire (*kāmadhātu*), the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), and the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*);
it is adorned with the seven treasures.
Within that wondrous palace, the altar site of ten cubits is these ten dharma-realms (*dharmadhātu*).
In the center of that site, upon the Greatly Awakened Lion Throne, there is the letter A, which transforms into a four-cubit *śarīra* (stūpa), which is the layered maṇḍala.
As for the most profound [aspect], it is the generation of the resolve and the practice toward Bodhi and Nirvana.

Above that is a great white lotus flower; upon this flower is the syllable *A*, which transforms into the body of the Dharmakāya Mahāvairocana Tathāgata. He utters the five syllables *A, Vaṃ, Raṃ, Haṃ, Khaṃ*, which transform into the bodies of the five Wisdom Tathāgatas. These further become the bodies of the eight petals and nine deities, and further become the bodies of the five Great Vidyārājas.

Mahāvairocana Tathāgata transforms into the syllable HAṂ; the syllable transforms into a sword; the sword transforms into the body of Acala Vidyārāja; and Acala Vidyārāja transforms into the great nāga Gokhara, manifesting a wrathful form while entwined with a sharp sword.
The Dragon King transformed himself into two messengers:
the messenger Siṃhala and the messenger Caṇḍāla.
These five syllables are called the Secret Siddhi; they are also called the Accomplishment Siddhi, and they are also called the Susiddhi.

Susiddhi refers to the universal accomplishment of the Buddha-fruit and the realization of Great Bodhi throughout the entire Dharma-realm. It is the secret language of the Dharma-realm, its radiance filling all places; only Buddhas and Buddhas can enter this gate, while Pratyekabuddhas and Śrāvakas cannot illuminate it. It is also called the Secret Siddhi.
If one recites it once, it is equivalent to having turned all the sutras one million times.
Regarding the secret siddhi, it extends from the heart to the crown of the head.
Secret siddhi is the accomplishment of the Dharmakāya; it is the treasury of the True Dharma consisting of the three eternal bodies.
Therefore, I bow my head in homage to Vairocana Buddha:
I bow my head to Vairocana Buddha, Who opens the pure eyes like a lotus flower,
The Tamer of the Three Realms, Teacher of Gods and Humans, The Savior of the World through the Great Bodhicitta.
The empowerment method of the profound and wondrous mantra flows into the gate of the letter A, which is non-arising.

The letter A is like the *amala-vijñāna*; the essence of the *amala-vijñāna* is the *ālaya-vijñāna*. In its function, the letter A contains and preserves all phenomena, just as the storehouse consciousness (*ālaya-vijñāna*) contains all dharmas.
Thus, the four characters of Vairocana contain the meaning of the four teachings (*catur-yāna*), and the nine-layered moon disc represents the eight petals and nine deities.
The mantra of Mañjuśrī for the lower-grade *siddhi* is: "A-ra-pa-ca-na.

The single character "Oṃ Jiliṃ" (Oṃ Ciliṃ) is universally applicable for all matters; this is called the "Emergent *Siddhi*" (*niḥsaraṇa-siddhi*). It is able to produce roots and stems that pervade the four directions. Reciting it once is equivalent to reciting the entire Tripiṭaka one hundred times. This emergent *siddhi* extends from the feet to the waist.
"Ami-ra-hūṃ-kha. This is the mantra of Mahāvairocana Tathāgata for the middling siddhi; it is called "entry into siddhi" (praveśa-siddhi).

It is able to produce branches and leaves. Furthermore, as for entry into siddhi: from the navel to the heart, light fills the four directions, radiating brilliantly, entering the Buddha-dharmadhātu; this is called entry into siddhi.
If one recites it once, it is equivalent to reciting the entire Tripitaka one thousand times.
The Vairocana mantra, "A VAṂ LAṂ HAṂ KHAṂ" (the supreme siddhi), consists of five syllables; this is called the Secret Siddhi, also known as Susiddhi, and also known as the Accomplishment Siddhi.
Regarding the secret *siddhi*: from the heart to the crown of the head; regarding the *susiddhi*: it is the accomplishment of the Dharmakāya. Furthermore, regarding the accomplishment of *siddhi*:

it is the accomplishment of the Buddha-fruit and the realization of Great Bodhi. It is the secret word of the Dharma-realm, its radiance pervading everywhere; only Buddhas and Buddhas can enter this gate. Pratyekabuddhas and Śrāvakas cannot illuminate it; thus it is named the secret *siddhi*.
If one recites it once, it is equivalent to having turned all the sutras one million times.
These three types of *siddhi* mantras, including the Heart Mantra of the Uṣṇīṣavijayā, are all the mantras of the three bodies of Mahāvairocana Tathāgata.
From this it should be understood that the Honored and Victorious Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa is the body of the Tathāgata Vairocana, and is the body of the Uṣṇīṣas of the three families.
As for the three consciousnesses: first, pātana, which refers to the six consciousnesses;
second, ādāna-vijñāna, which refers to the seventh consciousness.
Third, the *ālayavijñāna* refers to the eight consciousnesses.
Now, by adding the fourth—the *amala-vimala-viśuddha-vijñāna* (stainless, pure consciousness)—it constitutes the meaning of the ninefold core of the moon disc.

The *siddhi* of emergence consists of the roots and stems from the feet to the waist, which is the *nirmāṇakāya*; the *siddhi* of entry consists of the branches and leaves from the navel to the heart, which is the *saṃbhogakāya*; and the *siddhi* of accomplishment consists of [the parts] from the heart to the crown, which is the *dharmakāya* fruit of Buddhahood—all of these enter the stream of the syllable A, and one should practice the visualization in three stages.

Those of the highest grade possess bodies identical to the body of the Great Trichiliocosm, which is itself identical to the Dharmakāya of the Mahāvairocana Tathāgata. Within this Great Trichiliocosm, they preach the eighty-four thousand treasuries of the sublime teachings for the sake of all sentient beings, desiring to attain Buddhahood simultaneously with them.

In the middle grade of visualization, one contemplates the body of oneself and others as equal to the bodies within a medium chiliocosm; these are identical to the bodies of the Nirmāṇakāya Mahāvairocana Tathāgata. Within this medium chiliocosm, one preaches the eighty-four thousand treasuries of the Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings, desiring that they all attain Buddhahood simultaneously.

The lower-grade contemplation consists of my own body and so forth, which are bodies equal in size to a small chiliocosm; these are identical to the bodies of the Nirmāṇakāya Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva. Within this small chiliocosm, for the sake of all sentient beings, I preach the eighty-four thousand treasuries of the sūtras, desiring that we all attain Buddhahood simultaneously.

However, these three kinds of mantras are the most secret within secrets and the most esoteric within esoterica; those of the Two Vehicles, those who have broken the precepts, and those who lack faith find it difficult to enter this gate.

Those bodhisattvas with faithful hearts may recite and contemplate them day and night, and shall certainly attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Throughout immeasurable and innumerable kalpas, they shall be able to deliver all suffering sentient beings within the six realms, causing them all to enter into this syllable "A," severing all afflictions, delusions, and karmic actions throughout immeasurable and innumerable kalpas, inspiring them to give rise to the unsurpassed bodhicitta, and leading them all to realize the fruit of Buddhahood.

If there is a person of the highest faculties who constantly recites and maintains mindfulness during the three periods of day and night, or who at all times maintains moment-to-moment recollection, this person will certainly not abandon the body born of their parents; in this very life, they shall attain the inconceivable and rare Buddha-body.

If there is anyone who harbors such indeterminate doubts regarding this teaching, they shall fall into the Avīci Hell for immeasurable, inconceivable, countless, and incalculable great kalpas equal to the sands of the Ganges;
once those kalpas in that hell have finally ended, they shall again enter the eighteen hells and the eighty-four thousand hells;
thus passing through each of these successively until every kalpa is exhausted, they shall then fall among the hungry ghosts and the animals, remaining there until the end of their respective kalpas.

When the kalpa has ended and one is reborn among humans, because of a lack of faith in the Dharma, one suffers extreme poverty and intense suffering; throughout one’s entire life, one endures countless great illnesses, such that day and night pass without interval from this sickness and pain, and not a single virtue is cultivated.

After the end of life, one likewise falls into the Avīci Hell, where one constantly undergoes great anguish and is not born into a state of goodness. Therefore, for those who lack faith, it is impossible to speak of these three mantras as the excellent medicine for the fruit of the three bodies of the Buddha and the three types of bodhi.

If a person hears this mantra even once, and has planted immeasurable seeds of roots of goodness throughout their past lives, they shall likewise hear it now by virtue of the power of those past roots of goodness.

Such a person will certainly reach the end of their life and, in accordance with their vows, be reborn in the pure lands of the ten directions; there they shall preach this Dharma for the assembly of that land and for all sentient beings within the great trichiliocosm, further uprooting suffering and bestowing happiness so that they may realize the fruit of Great Bodhi. You should know that such a person is an emanation of the Tathāgata and is a bodhisattva; how much more so for one who recites it themselves and transmits the teaching to others—their merit is inconceivable.

If one recites this fifty hundred thousand times with pure faith, the immeasurable evil karma and transgressions accumulated throughout countless billions of kalpas since beginningless time will be forever extinguished. Following their wishes, after death, they shall be reborn within the Lotus Treasury World (*Padmagarbhalokadhātu*), where they will eternally behold the wondrous body of Vairocana Tathāgata—the original Buddha of the letter *A* of primordial awakening—and constantly enjoy the bliss of the Dharma within that world. This is the teaching from the golden mouth of Vairocana Tathāgata: the five wisdom Tathāgatas are born from within the letter *A*, manifesting infinite bodies. He who formerly heard the single character *A* is none other than the present Vairocana Tathāgata.
The One of Perfect Universal Knowledge with the mark of the white ūrṇā-kośa, Whose full radiance shines eternally like the sun and moon—
Akṣobhya, Ratnasaṃbhava, the Savior of the World, And Amitābha, the Sovereign of Amoghasiddhi— All,
within the auspicious wheel of *siddhi*, Transmit this wondrous Dharma to transform all beings.
Trailokyavijaya, sovereign of loving-kindness, Vajrasattva, the Immovable Honored One—
fulfilling your vow without fail at this appointed time, may you return to the Vajra once the yoga practice is complete.
Relying upon the Buddha Vairocana, I open the seal of mind-wisdom to establish this ritual standard;
with immeasurable merit universally adorning it, may all the Sugatas enter together into the dhāraṇī.
I pray that all practitioners who share this affinity may dwell securely in the unsurpassed ocean of purity.
One fascicle of the *Buddhoṣṇīṣavijayā-hṛdaya-narakabhedana-dharmaparyāya*. The postscript states:
"In the second year of the Enpō era, the year of the Dragon (Jia-yin), during the second month of spring, the brush was set to paper by the monk Chao-ran of Sōjikyō-ji Temple in Hokubu."
"Completed on the tenth day of the eighth month in the fifth year of Tenmei, the Year of Yi-si (1785), by the monk Jinin of Musashi, based on the original manuscript of Master Chōran.

In the seventh month of the year Xin-you (1801) of the era name Kyōwa, I sought out these various manuscripts at Chishakuin in Higashiyama, Kyoto. Daigen and others from Aizen-in on this same mountain transcribed them, collated them, and punctuated them with *kokuji* characters. Regarding the two aforementioned versions of the *Uṣṇīṣavijayā-dharani* and the *Pṛthivī-vivara-praveśa*, they were previously printed and recorded alongside three other versions of the *Uṣṇīṣavijayā*, which share the same ritual procedure (*siddhi-vidhi*) but differ in their textual lineages. Now, having re-collated them for carving into woodblocks, I await further comparison with superior manuscripts.
At Sōjiji on Mount Hōon, Kaidō’s Record of the Five Treasuries:
the liver is the red lotus, the Buddha Akṣobhya of the East.
The lungs: a blue lotus, representing Amitāyus Buddha of the western direction.
The heart: a yellow lotus, representing Ratnasambhava Buddha of the southern direction.
The kidneys: a red lotus, representing Śākyamuni Buddha of the northern direction.
Spleen: A white lotus with Mahāvairocana Tathāgata at its center. Liver:
The seed syllable HŪṂ; one forms the five-pronged vajra and makes offerings to the Honored One Akṣobhya of the East.
The heart seed-syllable, formed from a wish-fulfilling jewel, makes offerings to Ratnasambhava in the south.
The lung seed-syllable, formed from a vajra-lotus, makes offerings to Amitāyus in the west.
The seed-syllable *kṣi* forms the crossed-vajra (*viśvavajra*) for the offering to the Northern Lord Amoghasiddhi.
The seed-syllable *sphe* forms the golden stupa for the stūpa-offering (*stūpārcana*) of enjoying the Dharma-bliss within oneself.

The heart-wisdom, the Great Perfect Mirror Wisdom, resides in the eyes; the mind-wisdom, the Wisdom of Equality, resides in the forehead; the lung-wisdom, the Wisdom of Wondrous Observation, resides in the throat; and the kidney-wisdom, the Wisdom of Accomplishing What Is to Be Done, resides in the tongue.

The gallbladder is Trailokyavijaya; the large intestine is Kuṇḍalī; the bladder is Jvālāmukha; the small intestine is Vajrayakṣa; the spleen is Acala; and the triple burner is Samantabhadra, the Tathāgata who emits light from the ten directions to illuminate all buddha-fields.
The six repositories are: the gallbladder, the small intestine, the stomach, the bladder, and the triple burner.
